summary: Ice surface of each year 2016 to 2026 on the 3D strip: two swisstopo elevation models (2016, 2023), swisstopo lidar (26 tiles of 2021) and an elevation-band lowering shape fitted to five other glaciers for the years between and beyond. A model, not a measurement, except where a survey lies.

anchors.survey: GLAMOS volume-change table (release 2025, series file) lists this surface as source "sa3d-2023" with date_end 20169999: survey 2016, day unknown. Image strips over the strip in 2016 (swisstopo layer ch.swisstopo.lubis-bildstreifen): 2016-08-08 CRYOSPHERE MONITORING (24 % of ice cells, computed), 2016-08-26 CRYOSPHERE MONITORING (23 % of ice cells, computed), 2016-09-07 SWISSIMAGE (100 % of ice cells, computed). Which strip fed which cell is not published; the model puts the whole edition on one day.
anchors.placed_at: 2016-09-07 (a day a strip was flown, taken from the pair of flown days with the lowest ICESat-2 rmse (2.75 m); ties within 0.05 m go to the GLAMOS date if it is among them, else to the strip covering most ice. Chosen on the same shots as the check, so not independent. A2 was then set to the flight day of its lidar (see A2))

anchors.source: swissSURFACE3D raster (swisstopo lidar DSM, 0.5 m, read at 20 m)
anchors.survey: GPS times of the point clouds of 26 tiles read (tiles with ice). 20 tiles hold at least 85 % of their points on a single day (2021-10-10 on 12, 2021-10-11 on 8); 6 tiles were flown on several days within 60 days and take the point-weighted mean day (uncertain by up to about a month); 0 tiles flown on days further apart (or not read) are not used. The lidar sits on 100 % of the ice cells (computed).
anchors.placed_at: the flight day of each tile (see above)

anchors.source: swissALTI3D newest edition (2025 edition; swisstopo), which equals the swissSURFACE3D lidar of 2023 over the ice
anchors.survey: The edition equals the swissSURFACE3D raster of 2023 on the ice (median absolute difference under 0.05 m on every one of the 23 tiles with ice, computed). GPS times of the point clouds of 23 of these tiles (100 % of the 2023 ice cells, computed) were read: all 23 tiles with ice were flown only on 2023-08-19 (computed from the GPS times of their point clouds).
anchors.placed_at: 2023-08-19 (the flight day of that lidar; not a strip day: the best strip day of the year, chosen by the pair rule, lay 1 day later)

shape: Between two anchors the surface follows the lowering of each elevation band, from snow-off (1 May plus Bw/|Bs| x 153 d, melt even from 1 May: an assumption) to 30 September. GLAMOS has no band balance for Triftgletscher (BE). The band balance is a straight line in elevation fitted (computed, area weighted, 2200 to 3600 m) to the bins of Findel, Adler, Aletsch, Rhone and Corbassiere; it only decides how the change between two surveys is spread, the size comes from the surveys. Tried on the same ICESat-2 shots (rmse, computed): Findel 2.73 m (covers 93 %: not eligible); the borrowed line 2.75 m; Aletsch 2.89 m; Corbassiere 2.91 m; Rhone 3.41 m. 2026: the line is estimated from the glacier-wide Aletsch values of 2026 read from the GLAMOS figure (about +-100 mm w.e.). Beyond the last anchor (2024 to 2026) the rate of the last segment is applied to the measured 2023 surface, from the anchor difference smoothed over about 100 m (the raw difference carries noise and made 2024 to 2026 rough). The ground outside the 2023 outline stays at its 2023 height and no fade is applied, so a step grows along the outline (median lowering of the ice cells next to it 2.0 m in 2024, 3.6 m in 2025, 6.4 m in 2026, computed). Every cell stays between its two anchors or, outside them, within 2.5 times the lowering of its band at the nearest anchor.

validation.icesat2: ICESat-2 ATL06 v007: 465 shots on 2023 ice in 7 granules (July to October, slope under 20 degrees, quality 0, h_li_sigma under 1 m, inside the physical envelope). rmse 2.75 m over all years, bias +2.36 m (model minus shot), leave-one-granule-out: the A1 and A2 days are chosen on the other granules and the held-out granule is scored; with the days used 2.75 m. Per year (leave-one-granule-out): 2019 1.53 m (40 shots); 2020 3.71 m (41 shots); 2021 2.77 m (163 shots); 2024 3.61 m (54 shots); 2025 2.33 m (167 shots). Years without summer shots are not checked.
validation.datum: Heights are corrected with a plane fitted on 2412 shots on stable ground outside the ice (NMAD 1.96 m).
validation.not_checked: The split of the loss between years is an assumption (even melt from snow-off to 30 September); ICESat-2 scores years with shots, not each year step. 1 of 46 ASTER AST14DEM scenes (NASA LP DAAC, July to October 2016 to 2026) passed the gate (rock NMAD at most 15 m, at least 300 rock and 200 ice cells) in 2021; ASTER is rough, so only differences of a few metres mean something. No stake check: the GLAMOS point files of Triftgletscher (BE) (release 2025) hold readings of 2002 to 2003 only, none after the first survey (2016).

bed: Ice surfaces are not allowed below the bedrock: swissBEDROCK (swisstopo, 10 m; under glaciers swissALTI3D minus a modelled ice thickness, GLAMOS 2020) is the floor.
not_used: Airborne research DEMs and TanDEM-X series: the RAGMAC set covers Aletsch only (read); a first search for others is recorded in the source ledger of this glacier, and none was used; no radar surface was used. Years before 2016 are not modelled: older pictures use the 2016 surface.
licences: swisstopo open government data (swissALTI3D, swissSURFACE3D, image-strip footprints). A borrowed band balance and volume change: non-commercial (file headers). ICESat-2 (NASA, ATL06) and ASTER AST14DEM (NASA LP DAAC): used for checking only; the ASTER terms of use were not read. GLAMOS ice thickness release 2020 (radar beds, CC BY 4.0 per the landing page) and swissBEDROCK (swisstopo open government data): used for the ice bed checks.
caveat_2026: estimate: extrapolated like 2024-2025, with the 2026 balance estimated from the GLAMOS figure for Aletsch: provisional; not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots)

bed.lead: Three checks on Triftgletscher (BE) (all computed here, not source figures). The bed is the rock under the ice. "Radar bed" is the radar's own bed elevation (the survey surface minus the measured thickness, from the GLAMOS release); "model bed" is swissBEDROCK, which under glaciers is swissALTI3D minus a modelled GLAMOS ice thickness.
checks:
1 · Radar bed against model bed

At the 2,027 radar cells (20 m, median of the points in a cell), how far apart are the two beds?

Median −0.4 m over all cells, but it depends on the survey: −1.0 m (2008, 1,070 cells), +0.4 m (2012, 919 cells), −3.9 m (2002, 38 cells). Spread (standard deviation) 6.5 m in 2008, 5.4 m in 2012, 8.9 m in 2002; over all cells 91 % are within 10 m and 100 % within 30 m.

Reading: the 2012 survey agrees closest (93 % of its cells within 10 m) and the 2002 survey least (74 %). This is not a validation: the model bed was made from these same surveys (GLAMOS 2020 model, Grab et al. 2021), and at the survey lines it is the measured bed.

2 · One survey against another

Where two surveys covered the same spot, how well do they repeat?

Only 80 spots (25 m cells) have two survey dates (2008 and 2012: 68, 2002 and 2008: 1, 2002 and 2012: 8, 2002 and 2008: 3). The beds implied by the two surveys differ by a median +4.7 m (later minus earlier) with a standard deviation of 11.3 m; 59 % agree within 10 m.

Reading: enough spots for a rough measure of how the surveys repeat.

3 · Ground that is ice free now

Radar points where the newest swissALTI3D shows ground, not ice: the exposed ground is the bed.

166 points (166 from 2008) on 1 flight profile, ice about 71 m thick:

2008
Radar bed − ground now−4.7 m (−8.4 to −2.4)
Model bed − ground now−1.9 m (−5.2 to +1.5)

Median, in brackets the middle half (years with too few points are not shown). 22 % of the points have the radar bed above the ground now.

bed.read:
What this supports

  • At the margins the radar bed lies 4.7 m below the exposed ground and the model bed 1.9 m below it (medians of the points of 2008).

What it does not show

  • Few places: the 166 points lie on 1 flight profile, at the margins where the ice is about 71 m thick; deeper ice may behave differently.
  • No error band: the GLAMOS release has no uncertainty maps for the model bed, and swissBEDROCK's band under glaciers is about 0. Lakes, debris and the margin position (a few metres) were not screened.

How the points were chosen

  • In the 3D strip, at least 30 m outside the SGI2023 outline and 30 m inside the SGI2016 outline, so the model had ice there; newest swissALTI3D, slope at most 20°. With up to 30°: 402 points; with a 50 m margin: 15 points; with 100 m: none.

notes.uncertainty: Median over the ice of 2023, red whisker the 90th percentile (computed). The two swisstopo surveys carry 2.30 m (rmse of the 167 shots of 2025, the year with the lowest rmse among those with at least 100 shots; there are no usable shots in 2023, so this is an upper bound). The lidar of 2021 carries 2.30 m (the same as the surveys, because fewer than 30 shots lie within 45 days of the lidar day). swisstopo quotes 0.5 m below 2000 m and 1 to 3 m above (as quoted by Bannwart et al.), so the true value may be larger on a tongue this high. Between and beyond the surveys the error grows with the size of the change (factors 1.42 and 0.29), calibrated on the same ICESat-2 shots, so it is not independent; where a year has shots it is not below their rmse. Years without shots (2016, 2017, 2018, 2022, 2023) rest on the formula alone. 2026 has no value on the chart: it is an estimate (its balance is estimated from a figure for Aletsch), and its map in the viewer adds 25 % of its increment (median 3.4 m).
notes.sharing: Solid: the loss between two surveys is shared over the years by an elevation-band balance borrowed from five other glaciers (computed; GLAMOS has none for Triftgletscher (BE)). Dashed: extrapolated beyond the last survey (2026 with an estimated balance). Not used: measured years.
notes.independent: ICESat-2 also chose the survey days of both anchors and calibrated σ, so it is not independent (rmse is leave-one-granule-out). ASTER scenes are checks only (1 of 46 scenes usable; usable years: 2021). There are no stake readings for Triftgletscher (BE) after its first survey. Click a year for the numbers.

page.viewerText: The yearly surfaces in 3D with a year slider, the same viewer as for Aletsch. Switch on ICESat-2 shots (what the model was checked against) and hover a shot for its values; the bed and uncertainty colours are in the Colour menu. About 7 MB, loaded when you press the button.
page.mapcap: The model area = the 3D strip (outlined in black), as set in the walkthrough. Blue: ice inside the 2023 outline, about 12.9 km² (computed, 20 m cells). Red dashed: every cell modelled as ice, including ground that was ice at the 2016 survey, about 15.5 km² (computed). The 465 ICESat-2 shots used for the checks are shown in the 3D viewer (last section). The ICESat-2 check covers the cells within 1 km of a shot; the rest, 21 % of the modelled ice cells (7,605 of 35,419, computed), follows the same rules but has no check. Pictures of years before 2016 use the 2016 surface.
page.icesatNote: Also used to choose the survey days of both anchors, so not an independent check; the rmse is leave-one-granule-out (the days are chosen on the other granules).
page.asterNote: For scale: each used scene has a stable-terrain NMAD of 13.3 to 13.3 m (computed) (no used scene lies within 25 days of the 2023 anchor), so differences of a few metres are within ASTER's own scatter. rms = spread of the scene values of the year. Check only, not in the fit.
